Package neqsim.process.equipment.distillation

Class NaphtaliSandholmSolver

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.distillation.NaphtaliSandholmSolver
public class NaphtaliSandholmSolver extends Object
Naphtali-Sandholm simultaneous correction solver for distillation columns.

Solves the full MESH (Material balance, Equilibrium, Summation, Heat balance) system of equations simultaneously using Newton-Raphson iteration with block-tridiagonal Jacobian structure.

This solver handles wide-boiling-range systems where sequential substitution (tray-by-tray) methods diverge. The variable set per tray j is: liquid component flows l_{i,j} for each component i, temperature T_j, and vapor flow rate V_j. This gives (C+2) variables per tray for C components, and N*(C+2) total variables for N trays.

Reference: Naphtali, L.M. and Sandholm, D.P. (1971). "Multicomponent Separation Calculations by Linearization", AIChE Journal, 17(1), 148-153.

    • trayEta

      private double[] trayEta
      Per-stage Murphree efficiency cached at solver init time. trayEta[j] is forced to 1.0 for the reboiler (j=0) and the condenser (j=N-1 when present) so those stages remain rigorous equilibrium. Other stages use the value registered on the parent column via setMurphreeEfficiency(stage, value), defaulting to the global value when no per-stage override is set.

      The efficiency is embedded into the simultaneous MESH solution through the Edmister proxy K_eff[j][i] = K[j][i]^trayEta[j]. At trayEta = 1.0 the stage is rigorous equilibrium; at trayEta -> 0 the K-values approach 1.0 and the tray becomes passive (vapor passes through ~ unchanged), matching the behaviour of a heavily de-rated tray

      private double[] seedTemperature
      Per-tray seed temperature [K] used by the initializer when the tray is NOT fixed-T (i.e. T[j] is a Newton variable). NaN means "no seed, use Wilson estimate". This lets a user pass a reboiler T value as a hint when they specify boilup ratio instead of T as the actual MESH constraint.

    • enableBostonSullivan

      private boolean enableBostonSullivan
      Enable Boston-Sullivan inside-out refinement of the seed when at least one tray temperature is pinned (e.g. T-spec reboiler). The smooth Wilson BP seed misses sharp T-pinches; B-S inner loop (per-component tridiag MB + bubble-T) captures them and gives SR / Newton a sharper starting point. Auto-detected: only fires when fixedTemperature[j] is set on at least one tray. Default true.

    • hasReboiler

      Whether tray 0 is a reboiler with boilup ratio specification.

    • warmStartFromColumn

      private boolean warmStartFromColumn
      Whether to initialize the MESH variables from the converged column tray state.

    • componentImbalanceTolerance

      private double componentImbalanceTolerance
      Largest per-tray, per-component molar imbalance (relative to total feed) accepted by the early-exit branches.

      The early-exit branches historically gated only on computeMassBalanceError(), which is the overall column closure V[N-1] + L[0] = feed. That scalar is satisfied by profiles that leak one species from one tray into another, so a state with a large per-component imbalance was accepted as converged. Every early exit now also requires computeMaxComponentImbalance() to be within this tolerance.

    • hasCondenser

      private boolean hasCondenser
      Whether tray N-1 is a condenser with reflux ratio specification.

    • boilupRatio

      private double boilupRatio
      Boilup ratio for the reboiler (V/L leaving reboiler).

    • refluxRatio

      private double refluxRatio
      Reflux ratio for the condenser (L/D).

    • useOverallMBClosure

      private boolean useOverallMBClosure
      When true, the column uses overall mass balance closure L[0] = totalFeed - V[N-1] instead of V[0] = boilupRatio*L[0]. Enabled automatically when the user pins reboiler temperature but does not explicitly set a boilup ratio (i.e. boilupRatio is still the NeqSim default of 0.1). With pinned T, V[0] must be free to be determined by physics, not constrained to an arbitrary default ratio.

      Construct a solver with pre-saved original feed thermo systems and flow rates.

      double getLastTemperatureResidual()
      Get the latest temperature residual reported by the solver.

      This simultaneous-correction solver has no successive-substitution sweep, so it does not produce a tray-temperature change between iterations. It therefore reports Double.NaN and the column convergence gate falls back to the MESH residual vector, which is this solver's actual convergence measure. Reporting a fabricated zero here made DistillationColumn.solved() return true for solutions whose MESH material balance was grossly violated.

    • meshClosureAcceptable

      private boolean meshClosureAcceptable(String stageName)
      Check component material balances and the vapor-composition summation equation before accepting a shortcut state.

      A side draw exposes intermediate tray traffic as an external product, so trace-component closure must use the full solver tolerance rather than the legacy shortcut tolerance relative to total feed. Result materialization also requires sum(K*x)=1; otherwise normalizing the vapor composition rescales every vapor component flow. Newton's full residual already contains both equations. No-side-draw cases retain the established shortcut gate.

    • evaluateThermo

      private void evaluateThermo()
      Evaluate thermodynamic properties (K-values, enthalpies) at current state for all trays.

      V[j] is NOT recomputed here — it is a free variable of the solver. The vapor component flows v_{i,j} = K_{i,j} * x_{i,j} * V_j are computed from the current V[j] and K-values.

    • seedSolutionForDirectNewton

      private void seedSolutionForDirectNewton()
      Seed a mass-balanced initial guess for direct Newton entry.

      Used when useOverallMBClosure is active (T-spec'd reboiler with no boilup specification). Bypasses the BP-Wilson V-cascade — which is unstable for wide-boiling stripper topologies — and replaces it with a sweep that:

      1. Anchors V[N-1] (top vapor leaving column) to total feed minus a sensible bottoms estimate, so the overall MB closes.
      2. Distributes V[j] approximately linearly between feed trays.
      3. Computes L[j] from per-tray material balance: L[j] = L[j+1] + V[j-1] - V[j] + F_j (top down).
      4. Updates liq[j][i] from x[i] = z_i preserved-ratio normalization against L[j] (preserves the Rachford-Rice flash compositions set by initializeTrayState).

      Mass conservation is satisfied at the initial guess to within numerical tolerance; Newton then refines energy balance and equilibrium.

    • solveBubblePointMethod

      private boolean solveBubblePointMethod()
      Solve the column using the Bubble Point (BP) method (Wang-Henke, 1966).

      Decomposes the MESH equations into sequential subproblems: 1. Material balance: tridiagonal Thomas algorithm for each component 2. Summation: bubble point calculation for temperature on each tray 3. Energy: energy balance for vapor flow on each tray

      Returns:
      true if converged

    • phaseThreePHflashCorrection

      private void phaseThreePHflashCorrection()
      Phase 3: PH-flash temperature correction for energy balance.

      After the BP method converges on material balance/equilibrium, tray temperatures may be off because the BP method only solves MESH equations without the E (energy balance). This method computes the enthalpy of all streams entering each tray, mixes them, then PH-flashes to find the energy-consistent temperature. The resulting K-values and flows are fed back to the tridiagonal solver, and the process iterates until the temperature profile stabilizes.

    • solveSumRatesPhase

      private void solveSumRatesPhase()
      Sum-Rates (SR) energy balance correction phase.

      After the BP method converges on material balance, tray temperatures may be off because BP determines T from bubble-point (sum Kx = 1), which is inappropriate for wide-boiling / absorber-type columns. The SR method instead determines T from the energy balance:

      1. Compute EOS K-values and enthalpies at current T, x
      2. Tridiagonal M-solve for liquid compositions
      3. Update L from sum of liquid compositions
      4. Update V from total mass balance (bottom up)
      5. Correct T from energy balance using Newton dE/dT
      6. Iterate until energy + mass converge

      Reference: Seader, Henley & Roper, "Separation Process Principles", Chapter 10.4 — Sum-Rates method for absorber/stripper columns.

    • computeMaxRelativeEnergyError

      private double computeMaxRelativeEnergyError()
      Compute the maximum relative energy balance error across all non-fixed trays.

      The relative error for each tray is |E_j| / max(|H_out_j|, |H_in_j|). This gives a dimensionless metric comparable to the mass balance error fraction.

      Returns:
      maximum relative energy error (0.0 = perfect, 1.0 = 100% imbalance)

    • computeEnergyErrors

      private double[] computeEnergyErrors()
      Compute energy balance error for each tray.

      E_j = H_out_j - H_in_j. Incoming inter-tray phase flows are multiplied by the fraction remaining after the upstream side draw; the withdrawn fraction is an external product rather than traffic to the adjacent tray.

      Returns:
      array of energy-rate errors per tray in J/h

    • solveTridiagonalForComponent

      private void solveTridiagonalForComponent(int comp)
      Solve the tridiagonal material balance for a single component.

      For component i, the material balance on tray j gives: a_j * l_{i,j-1} + b_j * l_{i,j} + c_j * l_{i,j+1} = d_j, where a_j = -fV_{j-1}*K_{i,j-1}*V_{j-1}/L_{j-1}, b_j = 1 + K_{i,j}*V_j/L_j, and c_j = -fL_{j+1}. The factors fV and fL are the vapor and liquid fractions remaining as inter-tray traffic after any side draw.

      Parameters:
      comp - component index

    • computeResidual

      private double[] computeResidual()
      Compute the MESH residual vector.

      For each tray j, there are (C+2) equations:

      • C material balances: M_{i,j}
      • 1 energy balance: H_j
      • 1 summation equation: S_j (sum y - sum x = 0)

      Variable ordering per tray: [l_{0,j}, l_{1,j}, ..., l_{C-1,j}, T_j, V_j]

      Material balance for component i on tray j: M_{i,j} = l_{i,j}(1 + s_{i,j}) - l_{i,j-1} - v_{i,j+1} - f_{i,j} = 0 where s_{i,j} = K_{i,j} * V_j / L_j is the stripping factor, and v_{i,j} = K_{i,j} * l_{i,j} * V_j / L_j

      Energy balance for tray j: H_j = L_j*h_L_j + V_j*h_V_j - L_{j-1}*h_L_{j-1} - V_{j+1}*h_V_{j+1} - F_L_j*h_FL_j - F_V_j*h_FV_j - Q_j = 0

      Summation: S_j = sum_i(y_{i,j}) - 1 = sum_i(K_{i,j}*x_{i,j}) - 1 = 0

      Returns:
      residual vector of length N*(C+2)

    • computeJacobian

      private double[][] computeJacobian(double[] F0)
      Compute the Jacobian matrix numerically using finite differences.

      The Jacobian has block-tridiagonal structure. Only entries in the tri-diagonal bands are computed. For variable k on tray jj, we compute d(residual_j)/d(var_{jj,k}) for j in {jj-1, jj, jj+1}. After perturbing a variable on tray jj, only tray jj's thermo is re-evaluated (K-values, enthalpies depend only on local T and x).

      Parameters:
      F0 - current residual vector
      Returns:
      the Jacobian matrix [totalVars][totalVars]

    • refineJacobianBaseState

      private double[] refineJacobianBaseState(double[] initialResidual)
      Refine the derived tray state before a finite-difference Jacobian build.

      The primary Newton variables remain unchanged. Up to one full-column thermodynamic pass per local finite-difference variable is evaluated, matching the restore-evaluation budget that the frozen base replaces. The latest finite refreshed state is retained so the Jacobian base owns the most thermodynamically consistent K-value fixed point; the incoming derived state remains only as a fallback if no refinement is finite. Refinement stops early when consecutive residual vectors differ by no more than one tenth of the outer tolerance. This replaces the accidental, column-order-dependent K-value refinement that previously occurred while restoring each finite-difference perturbation.

      Parameters:
      initialResidual - residual at the current primary state
      Returns:
      residual owned by the retained derived thermodynamic state

    • applyMurphreeEfficiencyToK

      private void applyMurphreeEfficiencyToK(int j)
      Apply the Edmister Murphree-efficiency proxy to the K-values of tray j.

      The exact Murphree definition mixes the actual outlet vapor with the vapor entering from below: y_actual = y_in + eta * (y_eq - y_in). Embedding that into the simultaneous MESH solve requires the residual on tray j to couple to vap[j-1], which would expand the Jacobian bandwidth.

      The Edmister approximation K_eff = K^eta has the correct limits:

      • eta = 1.0 -> K_eff = K (rigorous equilibrium)
      • eta -> 0 -> K_eff -> 1.0, so y = K_eff*x -> x and the stage becomes passive (vapor leaves with the same composition as the liquid).
      This is the same correction used by many shortcut and equation-tearing column codes (e.g. ChemSep documentation, Edmister 1957) and is mass- and energy-balance consistent because the residual equations always use the scaled K[j][i].
      Parameters:
      j - tray index (0 = reboiler, N-1 = condenser when present)

    • runBostonSullivanRefinement

      private void runBostonSullivanRefinement()
      Boston-Sullivan inside-out refinement of the seed state.

      Activates when at least one tray has a fixed temperature spec — the case where the smooth Wilson BP cascade under-resolves a sharp T-pinch. The algorithm follows Boston & Sullivan (1974):

      1. Outer loop: compute base K-value Kb[j] as the x-weighted geometric mean of K[j][i], relative volatilities alpha[j][i] = K[j][i] / Kb[j], and an Antoine-style fit ln(Kb) = A - B/T via a Wilson-K perturbation at T + 5K.
      2. Inner loop (fixed alpha, A, B): solve one tridiagonal MB per component for x[j][i]; apply the bubble-point criterion sum(alpha * x) * Kb = 1 to get Kb_new; invert the Antoine fit for T_new; clamp T-pinned trays to fixedTemperature[j]; update liq[j][i] and vap[j][i] preserving the current L[j] and V[j] totals.
      3. Repeat until the relative change in alpha between outer iterations falls below tolerance.

      Mass balance is preserved by the tridiagonal solve. V[j] and L[j] are held at their BP-Wilson values; the downstream SR / Newton phase polishes the energy balance.

      private boolean computeSinglePhaseFugacityCoefficients(double[] composition, double tempK, double pressBar, boolean isVapor, double[] phiOut)
      Compute fugacity coefficients for a single phase (liquid or vapor) at given composition, temperature and pressure using a forced single-phase EOS root.

      Mirrors computeSinglePhaseEnthalpy(double[], double, double, boolean) — sets one phase, forces the requested phase type (GAS or LIQUID), and reads the fugacity coefficients directly. This is the correct way to evaluate K-values inside a column MESH residual, because K_i = phi_L(x) / phi_V(y) must be evaluated at the tray's actual compositions x and y, NOT at a flash composition.

      Parameters:

      tempK - temperature in Kelvin
      pressBar - pressure in bara
      isVapor - true to force vapor root, false to force liquid root
      phiOut - output array of length C to be populated with phi_i
      Returns:
      true on success, false if the forced-phase calculation failed

    • computeMassBalanceError

      private double computeMassBalanceError()
      Compute the overall mass balance error as a fraction of total feed.

      Products comprise the terminal vapor and liquid flows remaining after their tray splits plus every vapor and liquid side draw. This method returns the absolute product-versus-feed difference divided by total feed.

      Returns:
      mass balance error as a fraction (0.005 = 0.5%)

    • computeMaxComponentImbalance

      private double computeMaxComponentImbalance()
      Maximum per-tray, per-component molar imbalance, expressed relative to the total feed molar flow.

      For each tray j and component i this evaluates the MESH M-residual using only the fractions of liq[j+1][i] and vap[j-1][i] remaining after upstream side draws (the same equation that computeResidual() packs into the F vector), takes the absolute value, and divides by the total feed flow. Returning the worst value across all (j, i) pairs exposes leakage on individual species, which the scalar computeMassBalanceError() (overall column closure) and the L2 norm ||F|| can both mask.

      Returns:
      maximum relative component imbalance (1.0e-3 = 0.1%)

    • applyTrustRegion

      private double applyTrustRegion(double[] dx)
      Apply a trust-region clamp to the Newton direction dx (in-place).

      Limits each variable's per-iteration change to a physically reasonable magnitude to prevent Newton from leaving the basin of attraction. The whole step vector is scaled by the smallest acceptable ratio so the descent direction is preserved.

      Bounds: |dT| ≤ 10 K, |dV| ≤ 0.5*V + 0.05*flowScale, |d(liq_ij)| ≤ 0.5*liq_ij + 1e-3*flowScale.

      Parameters:
      dx - the Newton step (will be scaled in place)
      Returns:
      the trust-region scaling factor in (0, 1]

    • solveBlockTridiagonal

      private double[] solveBlockTridiagonal(double[][] J, double[] F)
      Solve the block-tridiagonal linear system J * dx = -F.

      The Jacobian J is block-tridiagonal with block size (C+2). Blocks: A_j (sub-diagonal, coupling to tray j-1), B_j (diagonal, tray j), C_j (super-diagonal, coupling to tray j+1).

      Uses the Thomas algorithm (block LU factorization) adapted for block matrices.

      Parameters:
      J - full Jacobian matrix
      F - residual vector (right-hand side is -F)
      Returns:
      solution vector dx, or null if singular

    • createAppliedPhaseSystem

      private SystemInterface createAppliedPhaseSystem(int trayIndex, double[] componentFlows, double fraction, PhaseType phaseType)
      Create an applied single-phase stream system from the solver's component flow inventory.

      Component flows are assigned atomically in mol/hr so normalization cannot change the accepted species inventory. The single-phase configuration is applied after init(0) because initialization may rebuild the phase list.

      phaseType - intended phase type

    • applyResultsToColumn

      private void applyResultsToColumn(UUID id, int iterations, double finalNorm, long startTime)
      Apply the converged solution back to the DistillationColumn trays.

      For each tray, creates a two-phase thermo system at the converged T, P, and overall composition for tray-state reporting. When a side draw is active, internal and side-product streams are materialized from the solver's vapor and liquid component-flow arrays so each split preserves the accepted species inventory exactly. Columns without side draws retain the established equilibrium-composition materialization path.

      Parameters:
      id - calculation identifier
      iterations - number of iterations performed
      finalNorm - final residual norm
      startTime - start time in nanoseconds
